items.title: Georgia governor's race essentially tied: AJC/UGA poll has Jackson 46, Bottoms 45; Quantus has Jackson +1.6
items.summary: Two new polls keep the race to succeed Brian Kemp a coin flip. The AJC poll (conducted by UGA's School of Public and International Affairs, published Oct 20): Rick Jackson (R) 46, Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) 45, 8% undecided, MoE +/-3.1; independents lean Bottoms 43-38. Quantus Insights (Oct 15-17, 755 LV, MoE +/-3.8, published Oct 19): Jackson 48.2, Bottoms 46.6, 4.5% undecided. Bottoms leads among Black voters (82-10 per Quantus), women, metro Atlanta and independents; Jackson leads among men, suburban and white voters, and voters 65+. If neither clears 50% on Nov 3, a Dec runoff decides it.
items.source_name: AJC (via Fox5 Atlanta) + USA Today + Quantus Insights

items.title: Spry Strategies TN governor poll: Blackburn 43.5, Green 32, Hatley 11.9
items.summary: Spry Strategies' statewide survey (635 likely TN voters, Oct 10-16, MoE +/-3.89): Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R) 43.5%, Jerri Green (D) 32.0%, independent David Hatley 11.9%, independent Lauren Pinkston 1.4%, ~10% undecided. Blackburn leads among both men and women and in every region (East/Middle/West TN), and dominates rural voters 53-18. 38.6% of voters have no opinion of or haven't heard of Green. Local analysis (TriStar Daily) flags the poll's GOP-tilted sample (53.3% Republicans vs 23.3% Democrats) and notes Hatley drawing ~12% could complicate Blackburn's path. Trump job approval in TN: 54.1-44.5.

items.title: Pell Center RI poll: Foulkes 39, Block 28, Guckian 17; lieutenant governor a dead heat
items.summary: Salve Regina University's Pell Center/Embold Research survey (815 likely RI voters, Oct 5-8, MoE +/-3.6): Helena Foulkes (D) 39%, independent Ken Block 28%, Republican Aaron Guckian 17%, 13% undecided in the governor's race. The lieutenant governor's race is a statistical tie: Sabina Matos (D) 43%, John Loughlin (R) 44%. Also: Sen. Jack Reed (D) leads 55-32; Kim Ahern leads the AG race 52-34. A second pollster (WPRI/Emerson, Oct 13: Foulkes 44-35, already in timeline) corroborates the race shape — Foulkes ahead but Block closing.
items.source_name: Salve Regina Pell Center + Political Wire

items.title: Sanders and O'Rourke bring early-voting tour to Texas; Talarico skips El Paso rally, holds own Fort Worth event
items.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders and Beto O'Rourke held two Texas rallies to kick off early voting. Monday night in El Paso (Abraham Chavez Theatre, with O'Rourke, Reps. Casar and Escobar): Talarico was absent, holding his own 'Clear Eyes, Full Hearts' tour rally at North Crowley High School in Fort Worth after a Denton stop; O'Rourke told the El Paso crowd $368M has been spent against Talarico; Sanders did not mention Talarico by name, focusing on billionaire donors. Tuesday (Oct 20) in Houston: Sanders, O'Rourke, Casar, Rep. Menefee and LG nominee Vikki Goodwin rallied at a black church near the University of Houston on day 2 of early voting; O'Rourke said Texas energy is 'even greater' than his 2018 run, citing Harris County's record 104.6K day-1 ballots.
